subject: Renewal: Reserved Pool Velocity + Add-on GPUs for Horizon Data
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir.rao@horizondatacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — reserved pool velocity & add-on GPUs

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the productive renewal check-in last week. Per Horizon's projected Q3-Q4 ramp, I put together a short proposal for the Dedicated renewal that aligns capacity with your traffic growth while preserving predictable unit economics. High level:

- Add-on: +8 x A100-equivalent GPUs to your primary reserved pool (pool id: HD-main).
- Term: extend 12 months from current renewal date (option to review at 9 months).
- Velocity SLO (proposed patch language): sustained reserved-pool throughput guarantee of 2,500 tokens/sec for the HD-main pool measured on 60s rolling windows (99.5% monthly availability). Burst allowance: up to 6,000 tokens/sec for 30s windows subject to instantaneous capacity; burst is not billed extra but not guaranteed beyond stated windows.
- Remedies: service credits equal to 5% of monthly Reserved fee if the velocity SLO is missed for more than 3 hours in a billing month (this is the draft we'd like to get onto the term sheet).

I've attached a short capacity forecast from your team and a draft SLA patch (redwood_draft_sla_patch_v2.docx). Pricing summary in the spreadsheet.

If this looks directionally right, can you confirm: (1) the +8 GPUs and 12-month term are acceptable, and (2) whether your procurement/legal team needs any alternate wording for credits vs. invoice adjustments?

Happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk through the SLO definitions.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0188

Attachments: Horizon_Demand_Report_Q1.pdf (summary), redwood_draft_sla_patch_v2.docx (SLA patch), capacity_pricing_summary.xlsx (pricing)

From: Samir Rao <samir.rao@horizondatacorp.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Li Chen <li.chen@horizondatacorp.com>, Horizon Data Procurement <procurement@horizondatacorp.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — reserved pool velocity & add-on GPUs

Olga —

Thanks, this is helpful and closer to what we discussed. A few clarifying items from our side before we loop procurement:

1) The +8 GPUs is fine; we do want the option to add another +4 mid-term on a 30-day notice if Q4 usage overshoots the forecast. Can Redwood support mid-term scaling with committed pricing?

2) On the velocity SLO: 2,500 tokens/sec sustained on 60s windows sounds reasonable. We need clearer measurement language for the SLO blackout windows (timezones and clock skew), and we prefer service credits applied to next invoice rather than cash refunds.

3) The burst allowance looks good; please also confirm whether KV-cache warming after model swaps is included in the velocity calculation or excluded.

Procurement (cc) — expect a redline on the SLA doc but this is the right direction. Li, can you review the pricing spreadsheet with finance and let us know any constraints?

—Samir
Director, Platform Engineering
Horizon Data
samir.rao@horizondatacorp.com

Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal planning — reserved pool velocity & add-on GPUs — internal draft

Team — forwarding Samir's feedback. Need quick alignment so I can send a near-final patch to procurement. Key asks: mid-term +4 GPU option at committed pricing, credits applied to invoice, clarify KV-cache exclusion.

Suggested edits to the SLA patch:
- Measurement: "Velocity SLO measured at the pool ingress, aggregated over 60s rolling windows in UTC. Clock skew tolerance: 5s. Metric reported as tokens/sec."
- Exclusions: "KV-cache priming and model load windows up to 120s per rotation per node shall be excluded from sustained velocity measurements."
- Remedies: "Service credits applied to the subsequent monthly invoice; credit calculation based on the percentage of the Reserved fee for the impacted month, capped at 25% per incident."

Pricing note for Marissa: if we include the mid-term add-on option (+4 GPUs) with committed pricing (pro-rated at 75% of the per-GPU monthly reserved rate for the remainder of the term), we should reflect that in the attachment.

Neha — legal flagged that they prefer 'service credits' vs. direct invoice refunds and want a cap on cumulative credits per year; I put a 25% cap in the suggested language. Any pushback on that?

Vivek — can you confirm the burst accounting approach? We should be explicit about burst being non-guaranteed and only applicable when pool headroom exists; also mention fallback to a smaller model variant if capacity constrained and that fallbacks will not be counted against the SLO.

Thanks — aiming to reply to Samir with a tracked patch by EOD tomorrow.

—Olga

Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal planning — reserved pool velocity & add-on GPUs — internal draft

Olga / team — quick technical confirmation:

- Burst accounting: we will meter sustainable velocity at the pool ingress. Bursts are allowed when pool headroom exists; bursts are not guaranteed and are excluded from SLO compliance calculations. We'll explicitly state: "Burst windows are excluded from sustained-velocity availability calculations."

- KV-cache/model-load exclusion: agree with exclusion up to 120s per rotation per node; additionally we'll exclude the first 5 minutes after major model rollout (version change) from SLO calculation.

- Fallback behavior: if capacity is constrained we will route to a compatible smaller model variant (explicitly enumerated in the term sheet). Traffic routed to fallback will not be counted against the velocity SLO for HD-main.

I'll have a short tracked-patch for the SLA doc by tomorrow morning.

Vivek

Redwood Inference
